title: RSAWIT International Marathon 2026 Review: Sibu Sarawak Full and Half Marathon
seo_title: RSAWIT Marathon 2026 Review | Sibu Sarawak Malaysia Race
meta_description: RSAWIT International Marathon 2026: November 22 at Sibu Town Square Sarawak. Full and half marathon with registration open.
dek: Set for 22 November 2026 at Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang (Sibu Town Square) in Sarawak, this RSAWIT-backed full and half marathon brings a flat course to Malaysian Borneo third-largest city. Registration is open.
verdict: The RSAWIT International Marathon stakes its claim as a Sarawak road race outside the Kuching mainstream, anchored at Sibu Town Square in a city defined by the Rajang River and a distinctive Foochow Chinese cultural identity. Two distances, 42.195K and 21.1K, cover the classic marathon spectrum without the shorter-distance filler that pads many event programmes. Sibu is built on the Rajang floodplain, which means a predominantly flat course profile. The November date places the race at the onset of Sarawak landas monsoon season, bringing higher rainfall probability to the Borneo coast, so wet-weather preparation should be part of every runner planning. The information maturity is the primary limitation: detailed logistics such as route maps and cut-off times are not yet available from a single authoritative source. For runners seeking a Sarawak marathon with open registration, a flat course, and Sibu riverside character rather than the more heavily marketed Kuching circuit, the RSAWIT International Marathon on 22 November 2026 is a bookable option worth considering.

sections.heading: Sibu: Sarawak Riverside Foochow City
paragraphs: Sibu is Sarawak third-largest city with a character entirely distinct from Kuching cosmopolitan waterfront or Miri oil-town bustle. Founded by Foochow Chinese settlers in the early 20th century, Sibu carries a cultural identity shaped by the Rajang River — Sarawak longest — which serves as the city economic artery, transport spine, and psychological centre of gravity [2]. The Rajang is a working river: barges loaded with timber, palm oil, and cargo move up and down its brown waters, giving Sibu an authenticity that more manicured destinations lack.

For a marathon runner, the relevant feature of Sibu is its topography: the city sits on the flat, low-lying Rajang floodplain, which means the course profile is likely to be about as flat as any marathon in Malaysian Borneo [1]. There are no significant hills — the elevation challenge comes from bridge crossings rather than sustained climbs. The town is compact, walkable, and affordable by Malaysian standards, with hotels clustered near the town centre and the race venue within easy reach of most accommodation.

sections.heading: Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang: Sibu Civic Square as Race Hub
paragraphs: Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang — Sibu Town Square — is the central civic plaza of Sibu, a large open space that hosts the city major public events and serves as the natural gathering point for a town-centre road race [1]. The town-square model has genuine advantages: the start line is visible from multiple approach angles, pre-race assembly does not depend on a single choke-point entrance, and post-race dispersal is naturally distributed rather than funneled through a single exit.

The square sits at the centre of Sibu commercial district, meaning hotels, restaurants, and race-morning breakfast options are within walking distance — a logistical simplicity that out-of-town races at remote venues cannot match. For runners travelling to Sibu, the race-morning routine is as simple as walking from the hotel to the start line.

sections.heading: The November Challenge: Sarawak Landas Season
paragraphs: The race date — 22 November — places the RSAWIT International Marathon at the beginning of Sarawak landas, the northeast monsoon season that runs from November through February and brings the heaviest rainfall of the year to the Borneo coast [3]. November is not the wettest month of the landas — December and January claim that — but it is the month when the weather pattern shifts, and runners should calibrate expectations accordingly: the probability of rain on race day is materially higher than it would be for an August or September race in Sarawak.

Temperature-wise, the landas brings slightly cooler conditions than the mid-year dry season, with start-line readings in the 24 to 26C range and daytime highs around 30 to 31C. Humidity remains high — 80 to 90 percent is typical — but the cloud cover associated with the monsoon can moderate the direct-sun exposure that makes tropical marathons punishing in the later kilometres. For the full marathon field, the combination of flat terrain and overcast skies can produce surprisingly fast times — provided runners manage their hydration and electrolyte intake for the humid conditions.

sections.heading: RSAWIT and the Sarawak Marathon Landscape
paragraphs: RSAWIT — a Sarawak-based palm oil company — lends its corporate backing to this marathon, placing it within the growing ecosystem of Malaysian corporate-sponsored road races that have expanded the country running calendar well beyond the flagship events in Kuala Lumpur and Kuching [1]. Corporate backing in the Malaysian race context typically means institutional funding for road closures, timing infrastructure, and race-kit production — the operational spending that separates a properly resourced marathon from a community fun run.

The Sarawak marathon landscape is dominated by the Kuching Marathon, which draws the largest field and the most international attention. The RSAWIT International Marathon in Sibu offers an alternative: a smaller field, a flatter course, and a more intimate town-centre experience in a city that most international runners have never visited. For the runner who has already ticked Kuching off the list — or who prefers a race where the start line is a five-minute walk from the hotel rather than a 30-minute Grab ride — Sibu represents a different kind of Sarawak marathon weekend.

sections.heading: Should You Run the RSAWIT International Marathon 2026?
paragraphs: If you are building a 2026 marathon calendar and want a Sarawak race with open registration, a flat course profile on the Rajang floodplain, and the character of a riverside Foochow city rather than the well-trodden Kuching circuit, the RSAWIT International Marathon in Sibu is a solid, bookable option. Two distances — 42K and 21K — cover the marathon and half marathon without the distraction of shorter fun-run categories, and Sibu Town Square provides a central, logistically straightforward race hub that makes the pre-race and post-race logistics simpler than they would be at a remote venue [1].

The caveat is information maturity: detailed logistics such as the route map, cut-off times, aid-station placement, and race-kit contents are not yet available from a single authoritative source. For runners who need full operational detail before committing — and particularly for anyone travelling from outside Sarawak — this is a gap. The November date also means the landas monsoon season, so wet-weather preparation should be part of every runner planning. For those willing to register now and monitor updates as race day approaches, mark 22 November 2026 at Sibu Town Square. This is a Sarawak marathon with a flat profile and a riverside character that the bigger-name races in Kuching cannot quite replicate.

faqs.question: Where is Sibu and what kind of race experience does it offer?
faqs.answer: Sibu is Sarawak third-largest city, located on the Rajang River roughly midway between Kuching and Miri on Borneo central coast. Sibu Town Square provides a central civic race hub with hotels, restaurants, and amenities within walking distance.
